_what_this_is: A committed floor for the outreach skip-list, and the only piece of send
state that survives a fresh container.
data/outreach_sent.csv is gitignored and has never been committed, because
it holds contact data. The Supabase mirror (public.outreach_sent) is the
durable copy — but _remote_emails() returns an EMPTY set when SUPABASE_PAT
is unset, and that is not an error, it is the documented offline mode. So a
fresh clone with no local log and no PAT resolves a skip-list of zero and
would cheerfully re-email all 571 superintendents already contacted.
This file makes that impossible without a deliberate override. It records
how many addresses we KNOW have been sent; send_outreach.py refuses to send
when the resolved skip-list is smaller than this, because a shrinking
skip-list means state was lost, never that people un-received an email.
Bump sent_total in the same commit as any wave that grows it.

sent_total counts SENDS; unique_emails counts distinct ADDRESSES. The guard compares against unique_emails because that is what the skip-list holds — comparing a send count to a set of addresses would trip forever the first time two districts shared one address.
note: 671 unique districts, 51.2% of Texas, zero duplicates (wave1-wave2 overlap verified 0). Waves before 2026-08-17 predate journey tracking and cannot be retrofitted; wave2-2026-08-17 is tracked.
